title: Cyrus and the Portrait
premise: Folklorist Xanthe Eriksen returns to the village of Hollowmere to record its forbidden songs, only to find Cyrus, the imaginary friend he invented as a child, waiting on his porch — unchanged after thirty years. Cyrus reveals the founders' ritual that keeps the village alive requires a living portrait painted from memory, and the last painter died mid-stroke a century ago. As Xanthe documents the songs, he realizes each verse he records erases a piece of his own identity, feeding the portrait's completion. In the end, Xanthe must choose: finish the painting and become the village's immortal, hollow guardian, or burn it and let Hollowmere finally die — he burns it, and walks out of the village as the songs forget him.
about_author: Cyrus Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote northern settlements before turning to fiction. They write horror rooted in folklore, obsessed with what communities agree never to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Songs Refused Twice
chapters.summary: Xanthe arrives in Hollowmere with recording equipment and scholarly confidence, but every villager goes silent when he asks about the founding hymns; old Marta sings one verse for him and then begs him to delete it. That night, Cyrus sits on his porch, exactly as a seven-year-old drew him. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as documentation begins to feel like trespass.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Xanthe finds the founders' ledger describing the Rite of the Portrait: a face painted purely from memory, renewed each generation, holding the village's death at bay. Cyrus admits he was the first portrait's model — and that Xanthe, as a child who imagined so vividly, was chosen before he was born. POV: Xanthe, with Cyrus's confession in dialogue. Emotional beat: the horror of discovering your childhood was someone else's design.

chapters.title: Every Verse a Piece of Me
chapters.summary: Compelled by dreams and Cyrus's gentle pressure, Xanthe collects all nine verses; with each recording, he loses something — his mother's face, his own name in his journal, the memory of why he came. The unfinished portrait in the chapel grows more lifelike, wearing his features. Villagers begin to smile at him with too many teeth. POV: Xanthe, fraying. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure, and the seductive relief of becoming less.

chapters.title: The Last Sitting
chapters.summary: At the solstice, the village gathers to complete the ritual; brush in hand, Xanthe sees Cyrus's true face beneath the friendly one — hungry, ancient, grateful. Instead of the final stroke, Xanthe sets the portrait alight. The village screams itself empty around him as decades of borrowed life collapse. He walks out at dawn, unable to remember his own name, carrying only a recorder full of songs no one will ever sing again. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: costly victory — survival purchased with identity, the price paid in full.
